findings.reason: the plan must name `review_report_directory` (or persist the snapshot path on the record) so the predicate does not re-spell the report-directory layout, the path-resolution duplicate the rubric calls out.
findings.text: §21 recomputes each stored review's unit digests from "the plan.html written beside its report", but the stored record built by `store_delivered_report` (`reckon/crew/plan_review.py:931-945`) carries no report or snapshot path, only `review_run_id`; the path is owned by `review_report_directory` (`reckon/crew/plan_review.py:791`), which the section does not name

findings.reason: the honest change is to call `_section_digests(snapshot_path)`; the section should say so, or state why the existing reader cannot be extended.
findings.text: §21 adds a private "snapshot read" though `_section_digests` (`reckon/crew/plan_review.py:296`) already accepts a `Path` and reads the document through `_as_document` (`reckon/crew/plan_review.py:205`), so a separate reader adds no behaviour the existing digest function lacks

findings.reason: an un-named text source lets the change measure re-extract prose and drift from the reader §16 built, the reuse the section must cite.
findings.text: §22 compares a unit's authored prose against the reviewed snapshot's text without naming `section_prose` (`reckon/_plan_html.py`), the one reader §16 places for authored unit text

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — §16's `section_prose` and §21's coverage predicate each hide substantial behaviour (slicing, skip-set subtraction, document-unit keying; snapshot recompute and per-unit join) behind one function, and the plan names each consumer.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §21 locates each stored review's `plan.html` snapshot without naming `review_report_directory`, the function that owns that path.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 1481, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; §16 retires public `strip_tags` for private `_strip_tags` in the same change that adds `section_prose`, and §21/§22/§23 each state no counted surface is added, so every section that touches a family names what it retires or why nothing is.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — §22 adds a word-level change measure over a unit's authored prose without naming the reader that owns that text, which §16 defines as `section_prose` on `reckon/_plan_html.py`.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — §21 introduces a private "snapshot read" though `_section_digests` already accepts a path and reads the document through `_as_document`.
